summary: Recursive call to expand_command_substitution after variable expansion causes infinite recursion on nested substitutions
failure_scenario: User runs 'echo $(echo $(echo test))' - inner substitution expands, then outer call re-expands it, recursing infinitely until stack overflow

summary: find_command_substitutions state machine doesn't handle quoted or escaped parentheses
failure_scenario: User runs 'echo $(echo "hello (world)")' - the ')' in quotes prematurely closes the substitution, causing incorrect parsing and wrong output

summary: Background pipeline creates dummy process that executes first command again, running it twice
failure_scenario: User runs 'sleep 10 | cat &' - sleep 10 runs once in background thread and again as dummy process for PID tracking, wasting resources and causing double side effects

summary: Background thread modifies global _LAST_EXIT_CODE while main thread continues, causing race condition on $?
failure_scenario: User runs 'sleep 1 &; echo $?' - $? may show background job's exit code instead of 0 because background thread overwrites _LAST_EXIT_CODE after main thread reads it

summary: builtin_source security check uses startswith which is bypassable via symlinks and directory traversal
failure_scenario: User runs 'cd /tmp; ln -s /etc/passwd myshellrc; source myshellrc' - realpath resolves to /etc/passwd which starts with /home/user (if cwd is /home/user), bypassing the allowed directory check

summary: Command substitution uses parse_line instead of shell=True, losing shell features like globbing and brace expansion
failure_scenario: User runs 'echo $(echo *.txt)' - globbing no longer expands in command substitution, outputting literal '*.txt' instead of matching files

summary: Background thread calls execute_pipeline which uses subprocess.Popen pipes, sharing global state with main thread causing corruption
failure_scenario: User runs 'sleep 5 | cat &' then immediately runs 'echo hello' - output may interleave, pipes may break, or file descriptors may conflict between threads

summary: shell_quote regex allows dangerous characters (backticks, $, !, ^) to pass through unquoted
failure_scenario: Job command containing backticks displays unquoted in 'jobs' output, misleading user about actual command that was run

summary: Aliases not expanded in command substitution because parse_line doesn't expand them before execution
failure_scenario: User defines 'alias ll="ls -l"' then runs 'echo $(ll)' - alias not expanded, command substitution fails with 'll: command not found'

summary: run_background_pipeline duplicates chain execution logic (&&/|| handling, pipeline execution) instead of calling execute()
failure_scenario: Bug fixes to execute() for logical operators or pipelines won't apply to background jobs, causing inconsistent behavior between foreground and background execution
